records.title: Vijayanagara at Hampi

citations.locator: Description; Outstanding Universal Value → Brief synthesis; property coordinates

records.title: Talikota: the aftermath at Hampi

citations.locator: Outstanding Universal Value → Brief synthesis, first paragraph; compare introductory description

details.heading: Origins and succession
details.text: Babur inherited Ferghana after his father’s death in 1494 and took Kabul in 1504. His Indian reign is only one phase of that longer career.

citations.locator: Opening biography; paragraphs on Ferghana and Kabul
citations.supports: Origins and succession and the specific statements in this section.

details.heading: Conquest and consolidation
details.text: Victories over Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526 and Rana Sanga’s confederacy at Khanwa in 1527 established his position. These events do not provide a digitizable border.

citations.locator: Indian campaigns: Panipat and Khanwah paragraphs
citations.supports: Conquest and consolidation and the specific statements in this section.

details.heading: Writing and evidence
details.text: His Chagatai Turkish memoir, the Baburnama, records campaigns, landscapes and personal judgments. It is a ruler’s own account and requires comparison with other evidence.

citations.supports: Writing and evidence and the specific statements in this section.

details.heading: Accession and alliances
details.text: Akbar succeeded as a minor in 1556 under Bayram Khan’s regency. The 1562 alliance with Bharmal of Amber helped integrate Rajput elites into imperial service; it did not mean every Rajput court submitted.

citations.supports: Accession and alliances and the specific statements in this section.

details.heading: Government
details.text: His administration developed revenue assessment and control of the nobility over years of experimentation. Abu’l-Fazl’s Ain-i Akbari describes the imperial system but also expresses its political ideals.

citations.locator: Political career: administrative reforms and Ain-e Akbari
citations.supports: Government and the specific statements in this section.

details.heading: Arts and translation

details.heading: Accession and diplomacy
details.text: The foundation’s timeline dates his coronation at Gogunda to 1572 and records Mughal diplomatic approaches before Haldighati.

citations.supports: Accession and diplomacy and the specific statements in this section.

details.heading: War and recovery
details.text: The timeline records Haldighati in 1576 and a Mewar victory at Dewair in 1582. It dates the new capital at Chawand to 1585. These are discrete events, not proof of fighting every year. The lineage page instead gives 1584 for Chawand; that discrepancy remains unresolved.
